20a19a at 1760×1175, drawn at 1530×1022 with ui_scale 1.15. The signal panel fills the full width again. Each row now has one action cluster on its title line: that source's actions (Todo, Trash, Accept, Decline) come first, then a divider, then Confirm, Wrong topic and Dismiss. Confirm lines up down the right edge, and the second line holds only the snippet and status. Day strip blocks are 44px tall, up from 26 (block-h), so when events overlap they split into lanes and each lane still fits a label: 2 lanes of 21px, or 3 of 13px. The bar above an overlap is orange where two events overlap and red where three do (conflict="triple": Acme call, Board prep and DD prep). Hours are labelled every hour.

19Gmail in Incoming · todo + archive, trash, unsubscribe, labels
19aGmail rows. Triage (Confirm, Wrong topic, Dismiss) is unchanged. After a divider come the Gmail-only actions: Todo… (e), Trash (#), and, when the email has a one-click unsubscribe header, Unsubscribe (⇧U). Trash also dismisses the email. Unsubscribe sends the one-click request and then trashes it. Both leave the row struck through with u undo, like Dismiss, and each acts on one email at a time. The category chip is the Gmail label: they sync both ways, and the tag icon means it's linked. There's no plain Archive. Archiving happens only through a todo (19b), so nothing leaves the Gmail inbox without a follow-up. Newsletters stay in the normal list.

19bTodo + archive. e opens a small form under the email: task text (the AI drafts it from the email), an optional due date, and the topic (pre-filled from the suggestion). The line underneath lists everything saving will do: add a task to the topic's Obsidian note (linked back to the email), apply the category's Gmail label, and archive the thread. ⌘↵ does all three through the outbox, and triage is done at the same time, because it now has a topic. Afterwards the row reads "Todo in … · archived", with Open task. Marco's row shows that state.

18Reclassifying a confirmed signal
18cChronology, redone. Selecting an entry adds nothing. ↵ (or a click) expands it in place to show its messages: sender colours, your replies, a faded context line before them, and Open in Slack. That's the missing "see more" step. Reclassifying is quiet: t moves the signal and s opens the split review (15g) for moving part of it. Both are listed in small text at the bottom of the expanded entry, not as buttons. Here the last message, about finops, is the reason you'd split.

18aFrom a topic's chronology. The selected entry gets two actions. Move to topic… (t) moves the whole signal. Review messages (↵) opens the split review from 15g in place, for moving only some messages. That appears only when the signal has more than one message. A moved signal leaves one quiet line where it was ("moved to Cloud costs", with u undo) until you leave the topic. A signal keeps one topic, and moving it changes nothing at the source.

17People · suggesting a new person, linking an account
17aNew person. When an unknown sender has shown up in enough signals (proposed: 3 or more in 7 days), the signal gets a dashed suggestion under its messages. The suggestion is separate from triage, so Confirm stays one key.

15A Slack signal the AI split across topics
What the code does today: suggest_topics can break one DM or thread into groups. The group with the newest message stays on the item and the rest become child items (parent_id), each filed under its own topic. In Incoming each piece shows up as an ordinary signal with nothing to say it's part of a larger conversation. In both options below, Confirm and Wrong topic act on this topic's messages only, and triage takes the same number of steps.
15hThe same view as 15g, for a channel with a thread. A thread's replies are indented under the thread's first message, behind a thin rule, which is Slack's own look, so indenting stays reserved for real threads. The AI treats a thread as one unit, so the whole thread lands in one group unless it's clearly split. Top-level channel messages group as they do in a DM. Each speaker's name gets their own colour (L 0.65). New here: d dismisses a message in place (10:40, with u undo). Confirm confirms only the groups that have a topic, so Unsorted (Marco's VPN message) stays in Incoming. j/k skips ⋯. t opens the usual topic picker, where you can also create a topic. The footer wraps to a second line when there are many groups.
Helm

15gGrouped by topic. Each topic's messages stay together, in time order within the group, and ⋯ marks where messages from other topics came in between. Moving a message with t sends it to its new group straight away, at its time position within that group. Here 10:04 has just moved from Unsorted into Acme outage, briefly tinted and with u undo. Groups are ordered by first message, so the conversation still roughly reads top to bottom. What you give up is seeing the whole back-and-forth in order, so g switches to In order (15f), keeping the same bars and footer. The choice is remembered across signals.

15dQuick check: a colour gutter per topic, with each group's Confirm off to the right. Colours: this topic is yellow (its category colour), Q4 headcount is orange, Unsorted is dashed grey. A topic that comes back later in the thread shows only its name on later runs, so its Confirm appears once. The trade-offs:
• Every work topic shares yellow, so any second or third topic needs a borrowed colour from the palette. There are only about two free (orange, aqua), and aqua already means "selected".
• Three sets of buttons sit on one signal, in a view that otherwise has one set per row.
• You triage other topics' messages from inside Acme outage, which blurs the topic-first layout.

14RSVP · Incoming, and a topic's Upcoming and Chronology
14aIncoming. An invite gets a second line with a no reply pill, Accept (y), Decline (n), Decline with note… (⇧N), and a yellow line naming what it overlaps: a meeting by title, or "Life" for personal busy time. Responding doesn't triage: the row stays until you Confirm, Wrong topic or Dismiss. Once you've answered, the line reads "Accepted · 10:58" with a link to change it in Google Calendar.

13Incoming · dismiss a signal, and where AI failures show
13aDismiss is added next to Wrong topic as a quiet ghost button, and d does the same. A dismissed signal stays in place, struck through, with Undo (u) until you move off it or the next refresh. After that it's gone from Incoming, with no topic link and nothing deleted at the source. It comes back only if the source gets new activity, like a new message or a status change. It works the same in Unsorted.

That tells apart the three cases the code can't today: never ran ("not run yet"), failed (this), and ran with nothing to suggest ("ok · nothing new"). A macOS notification fires once when suggestions start failing, not on every poll.

11Mac + iPhone · cross only through the services themselves, with receipts
No device link
The Mac and iPhone never talk to each other directly. Life comes in from a Proton Calendar Limited view link, which shows only busy times. Life goes out through Marvin's API into its Inbox, and the iPhone picks it up through Marvin's own sync. Replaces 10a's KDE Connect.
Receipts, then clear
A ~ line stays on the Mac until Marvin replies with the new task's ID. Only then is the line marked ✓ and cleared. If it fails, the line stays and says why. Nothing is ever deleted without that reply.
Work notes
A separate work Obsidian vault fits best, because Helm reads the files directly and no extra service sees them. Sync it only through storage your organization's BAA covers. Don't use Obsidian Sync or iCloud tied to your personal accounts.
11aNotes on the Mac, one second after ⌘↵. Work lines went to Incoming. The dentist line got its receipt, so it's marked ✓ and about to clear. The Sam line failed because Marvin was unreachable, so it stays on the page and will retry.

10Work laptop sees the shape of life, not its content
In
Your personal calendar's free/busy feed is the only thing that comes in. It's a URL that only carries times, with no titles. Helm draws those as untitled Life blocks, and they count down just like meetings. "Leave by" is worked out on the laptop from a travel buffer you set per block.
Out
A ~ line in Notes goes to your phone over KDE Connect when you send, and is then deleted from the laptop. Pressing ↵ on a Life block pings the phone to open that time in its calendar. Helm stores no personal account logins.
Stays out
Personal event titles, task lists and notes are never stored on the laptop and never reach the work AI. Blue work-calendar holds like Lunch and Walk stay as they are, because they already belong to work.
10aNotes on the work laptop. Physio and Pickup are now untitled Life blocks, with a leave-by tick before Pickup. Physio is selected, and its popover shows everything the laptop knows. The dentist line now starts with ~ and goes to the phone.

9Notes and Reflect tabs · three kinds of todo
Your notebook glyphs
Do · square, blue · [] Research · circle, green, no outcome needed · () Delegated · triangle, red, with a name · ^ @name Note · dash · -
The glyph's shape carries the meaning, so the blue and green here can't be mistaken for the Personal and Jobs category bars.
Notes
A writing surface, not a todo list. Type freely; lines break out into suggested topics, people or apps (Marvin / Jira) in a margin, and one send drops them into Incoming. A delegated line can offer a Jira task, but doesn't have to become one. The paper notebook stays separate. Super+J captures from anywhere.
Reflect
Built to stop, so there's no day strip, search or assistant pane; only a small countdown pill when a meeting is near. The app nudges you into it at the end of the day (9d). Day · Week · Month · Quarter each write their own Obsidian note, and each level rolls up the one below. Carry forward works like bullet-journal migration: > tomorrow, < schedule, or × let go, with no guilt language.
9aNotes, rebuilt as a writing page. You just type, and prefixes become glyphs. A fixed "Goes to" margin quietly suggests a topic, person or app for each line, all left-aligned in one column. Tab on a line changes it. One send moves everything into Incoming, where the real triage happens.

7Topic view: color back, sections separated, Open first
Color, in three layers
Your categories keep the kitty yellow, blue, purple and green. App icons are real image files in icons/, shown with a 60% desaturation filter. The ones there now are placeholders; overwrite them with actual app icons or your own. The interface itself (selection, active tab, today's links) uses gruvbox aqua (#8ec07c), which none of your categories use.
Marvin Gmail (work) Slack Jira Google Cal Obsidian Sheets Notion Proton Mail (personal) Proton Cal
Sections that don't bleed
Each section is its own raised panel with a header bar: icon, label and count. Panel steps are gruvbox bg0 (#282828) on bg0_h (#1d2021) with a bg1 edge, so the panels read as separate before you read a word. The chronology is back to the timeline, with a line, dots and app icons.
Day strip
All blocks are faded. Meetings on the current topic today come back to full strength with an aqua ring. When a topic has none today, a note on the right says so and names the next one (7b). Order in the left column: Upcoming (only when something is soon) → Open → Chronology → People.

Solid dots are things that happened; open dots are upcoming or not done yet. App icons are image files in icons/, so you can drop in real ones.

Structure
Incoming · Priorities · Topics, plus search (/). Unsorted is now a group inside Incoming. Mail groups became topics, so alert mail lives on a topic and its bulk actions write back from there. 4Incoming, Unsorted, Mail groups, Priorities → Topic
Five views, one app
The tabs go Incoming (triage) · Priorities · Topic (what a card opens) · Unsorted · Mail groups. The date and clock are gone; the calendar column carries a live countdown to the next meeting, counted in minutes. On-screen helper text is removed.
Reclassify is feedback
Reclassify sends the item to Unsorted and tells the model which signal made the wrong link (a thread, a sender, a keyword). It then suggests again with that correction applied. You pick the topic manually, or accept the new suggestion.
Mail write-back, never automatic
Mail groups is where bulk mail gets explored. Every action you take writes back to Thunderbird: move, mark read, delete to Trash, or create a filter. Each shows its exact count first and offers undo. The assistant can propose an action from plain language, but it only previews; you run it. Nothing is ever deleted by the app on its own.
4aIncoming. New items grouped by topic, then by mail group, with Unsorted listed separately. One reclassified row shows what happens after you press Reclassify. The calendar highlights this topic's meetings and counts down to the next one.

3Topics as the root, plus an urgency × importance lens
The graph
A topic is the root. Meetings, mail, Slack summaries, tickets, tasks, and notes hang off it. So do people, who have their own notes and link to meetings and topics too. Selecting a topic lights up its meetings on the day column.
Triage by topic
New items land in the topic the app thinks they belong to. Open the topic to see what's new, then Confirm or Reclassify each one. Reclassify moves the item to Unsorted without asking anything, and the topic keeps its context. Bulk and FYI mail never enter the list.
Urgency ≠ importance
Scoring works like TaskWarrior. Urgency comes from due dates, how long something has waited on you, meetings coming up, and who's asking. Importance comes from your category, a topic flag, and manual bumps. Every score shows its reasons, so you can disagree with it.
3aTopics. Left: topics sorted by urgency, with new-item counts. Middle: the selected topic, showing what's new (confirm / reclassify), its people, and its meetings. Right: the day to scale, with this topic's meetings highlighted. The assistant starts collapsed here, since this is triage.

1Four concepts: one desktop window, dashboard + collapsible assistant pane
Brief, as I understood it
You're a manager moving into a director role. Your day is mostly meetings, plus decisions, escalations, and things you're waiting on from others, with personal life mixed in. This is a KDE window, keyboard-first and dense. The dashboard is primary; chat sits beside it and only suggests. Slack is held and delivered in the gaps between meetings. Time to the next meeting is always visible, and the day's plan is logged against what actually happened.
How the assistant gets context
No pinning. The app keeps a local index of every source that refreshes on each sync. You reference things explicitly with @ (@Priya, @PLAT-1187, @11:00). Otherwise it retrieves on its own and cites what it used, each with a sync time. Stale sources are flagged in the answer itself. Longer outputs (briefs, reviews) are written to Obsidian as notes.
Color is a first-class system
There are two layers of color. Sources get a tinted code chip. Your categories (synced from Marvin categories and Thunderbird tags, same hue everywhere) get a dot or bar. All colors share one lightness and chroma, so they read as a set against Nocturne's quiet ground.
